rounds.text: Savita Oil Technologies Ltd is demonstrating a powerful acceleration in fundamental performance, highlighted by a TTM compounded sales growth of 26% and a staggering 222% compounded profit growth over the same period [E16, E19]. This momentum is validated by an elite relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 alongside technical positioning that has the price trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E48, E49]. Operating profitability is expanding dramatically, evidenced by a quarterly operating margin reaching 25% in June 2026 compared to just 6% in the year-ago quarter [E28]. Furthermore, the business boasts rock-solid financial health with a 0.00x debt-to-equity ratio, nil borrowings, and substantial cash, cash equivalents, and investments totaling near Rs 508 crores as of March 31, 2026 [E35, E79, E80]. Operational execution is equally robust, backed by double-digit volume growth across all divisions in Q4 FY26 and participation in high-growth secular frontiers like immersion coolants, which address surging data center demands [E74, E75]. Domestic institutions have recognized these merits, increasing their stake to 13.18% by June 2026 from 7.42% in September 2023, driving positive institutional money flow [E41, E42]. Conceded: the DCF intrinsic value estimate sits at Rs 668 per share against a market price of Rs 761, resulting in a negative margin of safety [E43, E44].

The valuation of Savita Oil Technologies is detached from its historical fundamental reality, evidenced by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 668 per share against a market price of Rs 761, creating a negative margin of safety of -13.9% [E43, E44]. Long-term profit growth fails to justify the current price, with compounded profit growth over 5 years at -9% and over 3 years at -13% [E17, E18], contrasting sharply with a 5-year share price growth of 21% [E21] to highlight a classic price-led disconnect [E54]. Furthermore, the company delivers weak returns on equity, registering an 8.3% ROE in filed statements and a median ROE of just 8% over the last 3 years and last year [E13, E25, E26], while trading at an expensive price-to-book ratio of 2.95x against a sector benchmark of 1.8x [E7]. Operational risks are compounded by inconsistent operating margins over recent years and quarters [E29, E30], alongside management explicitly citing significant daily volatility in key feedstock supplies [E81]. Conceded: the company maintains a strong balance sheet with zero or near-zero borrowings and robust short-term liquidity [E35, E36, E79], plus high recent institutional accumulation [E41, E42].

Conceded: a discounted cash flow puts intrinsic value at Rs 668 per share against a market price of Rs 761 with a negative margin of safety of -13.9% [E43, E44], and 5-year and 3-year compounded profit growth sit at -9% and -13% [E17, E18]. However, looking backward at multi-year averages completely misses the explosive inflection occurring right now, evidenced by trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth of 222% [E19] and quarterly operating margins surging to 25% in June 2026 compared to 6% a year prior [E28]. While historical ROE figures are cited, the underlying balance sheet is pristine with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x alongside strong recent free cash flow of Rs 107 Cr in March 2026 [E33, E35]. Conceded: operating margins have been historically inconsistent [E29, E30] and management notes feedstock volatility [E81], yet domestic institutional investors have aggressively increased their stake from 7.42% to 13.18% [E41], confirming that sophisticated capital is aggressively front-running the massive volume expansion and margin acceleration happening across all operating divisions [E74].

Conceded: domestic institutional investors increased their stake from 7.42% to 13.18% [E41]. However, this institutional accumulation is overshadowed by the fact that promoters have simultaneously reduced their holdings from 7.19% to 68.93% and foreign institutions have pulled back from 1.73% to 1.02% [E39, E40]. While the bull highlights trailing twelve-month profit growth of 222% [E19], this dramatic spike occurs against a backdrop where 5-year and 3-year compounded profit growth are severely negative at -9% and -13% [E17, E18], and median return on equity over the last 3 years languishes at a low 8% [E25]. The bull points to June 2026 quarterly operating margins reaching 25% [E28], but ignores the official company guidance noting significant daily volatility in key feedstock supplies [E81], which directly threatens the sustainability of such margins. Furthermore, the company's own historical yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are officially classified as inconsistent [E29, E30]. Finally, despite a pristine debt-to-equity ratio [E35], borrowings have crept up from zero to Rs 2 Cr in March 2026 [E37], and the stock trades at an expensive 2.95x price-to-book ratio against a sector benchmark of just 1.8x [E7].

Conceded: promoters reduced holdings from 7.19% to 68.93% and foreign institutions moved from 1.73% to 1.02% [E39, E40]. However, domestic institutions aggressively accumulated shares, expanding their stake from 7.42% to 13.18% [E41], and institutional money flow reads positive [E42]. While historical multi-year profit growth showed negative figures [E17, E18], the trailing twelve-month period delivered an explosive 222% profit surge alongside a 26% increase in sales growth [E16, E19]. The bear cites feedstock volatility [E81], yet ignores that the company reported double-digit volume growth across all divisions in Q4 FY26 [E74] and achieved a dramatic 25% operating margin in June 2026 [E28]. Conceded: borrowings crept up to Rs 2 Cr [E37], but the company remains virtually debt-free with a pristine 0.00x debt-to-equity ratio [E35], substantial cash and investments of roughly Rs 508 crores [E80], and a robust current ratio of 2.53x [E36].

Conceded: domestic institutions increased their stake to 13.18% [E41] and institutional money flow is positive [E42]. However, the bull's focus on recent short-term surges ignores the persistent structural weakness of a 5-year compounded profit growth of -9% and a 3-year drop of -13% [E17, E18]. Conceded: the company reported double-digit volume growth in Q4 FY26 [E74] and a high operating margin in June 2026 [E28], yet the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are officially categorized as "Inconsistent" [E29, E30]. While the bull highlights the massive TTM profit spike [E19], it glosses over the fundamental valuation disconnect where a DCF model calculates an intrinsic value of only Rs 668 against a higher market price [E43], resulting in a negative margin of safety of -13.9% [E44]. Furthermore, the bull minimizes feedstock volatility, whereas management itself explicitly warns of significant daily volatility in key supplies [E81], and insiders—represented by promoters—have steadily reduced their holdings from 71.92% to 68.93% [E39].
